title: GB200 NVL72 two-tier memory: HBM3E vs LPDDR5X behind NVLink-C2C (rack level)

units.bandwidth_tbps: TB/s (as printed; aggregate peak across rack)
units.gbps_per_gb: GB/s per GB (= bandwidth_tbps / capacity_tb, TB cancels)

conventions: Rack-level column of NVIDIA's GB200 NVL72 spec table (72 GPUs, 36 Grace CPUs). Decimal units: 1 TB = 1000 GB. Bandwidths are vendor peak specs. gbps_per_gb = (bandwidth_tbps*1000)/(capacity_tb*1000).

nvidia_spec.cite: NVIDIA, GB200 NVL72 product page, Specifications table
nvidia_spec.locator: Specifications table, rows 'GPU Memory | Bandwidth' and 'CPU Memory | Bandwidth', column GB200 NVL72 (rack)

rows.loc: Specs table, 'GPU Memory | Bandwidth': '13.4 TB HBM3E | 576 TB/s' (NVL72 column)
rows.unc: capacity and bandwidth: exact (vendor spec, printed); gbps_per_gb derived: 576/13.4 = 42.99
rows.note: Per-superchip-side column on same page: 372 GB HBM3E | 16 TB/s (16000/372 = 43.0 GB/s per GB, consistent).

rows.attach: Grace CPU LPDDR5X, reached from GPUs over NVLink-C2C (CPU memory)
rows.loc: Specs table, 'CPU Memory | Bandwidth': '17 TB LPDDR5X | 14 TB/s' (NVL72 column)
rows.unc: capacity and bandwidth: exact (vendor spec, printed); gbps_per_gb derived: 14/17 = 0.8235
rows.note: Per-superchip column on same page: 'Up to 480 GB LPDDR5X | Up to 512 GB/s' (512/480 = 1.07 GB/s per GB). This differs from the rack figure (14 TB/s / 36 CPUs = ~389 GB/s each; 17 TB / 36 = ~472 GB each), so the 0.82 depends on using the rack-level row; the page does not reconcile the two.

extraction.method: Parsed saved HTML fulltext/gb200-nvl72-nvidia.html (tags stripped) and read spec table text directly; arithmetic by hand/python. Notes not consulted.

caveats: Vendor spec, peak bandwidth, not measured.
LPDDR5X is a capacity tier by role, not 'far away'; GPU access goes via NVLink-C2C, whose per-GPU link speed is not given in this table.
Rack-level LPDDR5X (14 TB/s, 17 TB) and per-superchip (512 GB/s, 480 GB) rows are not perfectly consistent when divided by 36; the ratio 0.82 uses rack numbers as printed.
Page footnote: some compute rows are sparse specs; memory rows carry no footnote.
